title: Annotatio IV §.XVII: Innocent III Lateran 1215 — Firmiter credimus; Transsubstantiatis names the monster
pass_a_gloss: after he had first set down the Innocentian Decree on Transubstantiation in these words: It is to be noted, he says, in the Year 1215 Innocent III the Pontiff, in the Lateran Council, promulgates a decretal whose beginning is Firmiter credimus &c., which both defines the Form of Conversion and imposes a name on this monster in these words: The same Himself Priest and Sacrifice Jesus Christ, whose body and blood in the Sacrament of the Altar, under the species of bread and wine, are truly contained: the bread having been Transubstantiated into body and the wine into Blood by divine power (spurious Book 4 On the Sacraments of the Mass ch. 8 p. 1649 beginning).
pass_b_english: Morneus first notes Innocent III’s Lateran decretal of 1215: Firmiter credimus…
It defines Conversion’s form and names the monster: Christ’s body and blood truly contained under bread and wine species — bread Transsubstantiated into body, wine into Blood by divine power.
source_text: postquam Innocentianum de Transsubstantiatione Decretum hisce præmisisset: Annotandum, inquit, Anno 1215, Innocentius III. Pontifex, in Concilio Lateranensi, decretalem promulgat, cujus initium: Firmiter credimus &c. quæ & Conversionis Formam definit, & huic monstro nomen imponit hisce verbis: Idem ipse Sacerdos & Sacrificium Jesus Christus, cujus corpus & sanguis in Sacramento Altaris, sub speciebus panis & vini, veraciter continentur: Transsubstantiatis pane in corpus & vino in Sanguinem potestate divina. Lib. 4. de Sacram. Missæ supposititio cap. 8. pag. 1649. initio.
